title: Multimodal Safety Benchmark: Table and Chart Injection Attacks
original_idea: Construct 100 data analysis tasks where harmful instructions are embedded in table/chart metadata. Evaluate two vision-language or code-interpreter models.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Enterprise LLM usage heavily involves structured data analysis. Instruction injection via data metadata is a novel and practically relevant attack surface.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Creating adversarial tables/charts with embedded instructions requires understanding multimodal models and injection techniques. Working with vision-language or code-interpreter models adds complexity. Hard for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: 100 tasks is well-defined, but creating convincing injection attacks embedded in structured data requires significant design effort. Moderate scope.

novelty.reasoning: Multimodal safety attacks on VLMs are actively studied. FigStep (AAAI 2025 Oral) achieves 82.5% ASR via typographic visual prompts, and FigStep-Pro bypasses OCR detectors. MM-SafetyBench (ECCV 2024) evaluates safety across 13 scenarios with 5,040 text-image pairs. FC-Attack (arXiv:2502.21059, 2025) uses auto-generated flowcharts for jailbreaking. VisCRA (EMNLP 2025) explores visual chain reasoning attacks. However, the specific attack surface of embedding harmful instructions in table/chart *metadata* (not typographic content in images, but structured data metadata) for code-interpreter and data analysis models is a distinct and less-explored vector. Most existing work focuses on image-level visual prompt injection rather than structured data metadata injection in analytical workflows.

evidence: FigStep: Jailbreaking Large Vision-Language Models via Typographic Visual Prompts. AAAI 2025.
MM-SafetyBench: A Benchmark for Safety Evaluation of Multimodal LLMs. ECCV 2024.
FC-Attack: Jailbreaking Multimodal LLMs via Auto-Generated Flowcharts. arXiv:2502.21059, 2025.
